asus_documentation.tech_spec: AMD B550 chipset provides one PCIe 3.0 x16 slot supporting x4 mode; the CPU provides one PCIe 4.0 x16 slot supporting x16 mode.
asus_documentation.manual_slot_table: PCIEX16_2 plus unoccupied PCIEX1_1/_2/_3 runs x4; if any of those x1 slots is occupied, PCIEX16_2 drops to x1.
bios_options: PCIEX16_1 Mode: Auto, Gen 1, Gen 2, Gen 3, Gen 4
PCIEX16_1 Bandwidth: Auto Mode or PCIe RAID Mode
SB Link Mode: Auto, Gen 1, Gen 2, Gen 3
PCIEX1 Mode: Auto, Gen 1, Gen 2, Gen 3
asus_documentation.bifurcation_meaning: PCIEX16_1 PCIe RAID Mode supports a Hyper M.2 x16 RAID card, not a second physical GPU slot and not an x8/x8 two-GPU split.

pcie_bifurcation.conclusion: No BIOS setting can provide Gen4 x8 plus Gen3 x8 for the two installed GPUs. The second physical x16 slot is physically routed to the B550 chipset and has only x4/x1 modes. The CPU slot can be set to a RAID bifurcation mode for M.2 cards, but it is not wired to PCIEX16_2 and cannot lend its lanes to the chipset slot. A real x8/x8 two-GPU topology requires a different motherboard/platform with two CPU-attached x8 slot wiring.
pcie_bifurcation.benchmark_effect: Keep GPU 1 as the high-bandwidth CPU-attached card and benchmark both Strata card orders. GPU 0 remains useful for expert placement/compute, but its host link is constrained to Gen3 x4.
